messages:
anya: Heads-up — bringing up sparrowx14b (14B v2-opt4) on int4 for hosted canary. Seeing decent perf but a recurring OOM pattern when requests use long max_new_tokens (>=256).
kai: Thanks — can you paste the perf + OOM trace? Also which quant config?
anya: Quick numbers from a small cluster of p4d nodes: 1) int4 inference throughput: ~220 tok/s per GPU at seq_len=1024, batch=4. 2) Latency p95 ~340ms on short prompts. 3) OOMs triggered when a single request has max_new_tokens>=256 and payload has long context (~2k).
anya: Repro log snippet:
```
[2026-02-18 14:22:10] request id=abc123 model=sparrowx14b quant=int4 seq=2048 max_new_tokens=320 mem_before=78.1GB mem_after=84.4GB -> OOM
Trace: kv_cache_alloc failed at reserve_blocks
```
anya: Model was converted with our standard int4 recipe (group=128, clip=0.997). Quality on eval harness: MMLU-like subset down ~1.1% vs fp16; GLUE-ish parity ~0.3%.
drew: Could be KV cache blowup + fragmentation. Have you tried smaller per-request max_new_tokens default? Also what's batching config?
anya: Default route config used: `batch_max_tokens=4096`, `max_concurrent_requests=8`, `microbatch_size=1`. For these long-gen requests, batching pushes aggregate KV pressure.
ml-oncall: Suggestion: reduce route default `max_new_tokens` to 192 for sparrowx14b-int4 as a temporary mitigation and enable `kv_trim_threshold=0.85` for canary. That buys headroom and reduces fragmentation.
anya: Did a quick canary tweak: set max_new_tokens default=192, microbatch_size=2, reduced batch_max_tokens to 3072. Result: no OOMs in 1h soak under our synthetic long-context traffic; throughput fell ~8% but p95 latency stable.
bench-bot: Canary perf dashboard: https://bench.redwood.internal/sparrowx14b/int4/canary/3191234567 -> shows baseline vs canary curves.
kai: OK — two actionable items: 1) Roll route default change (192) + kv_trim for canary; 2) Run quant-sensitivity eval across our 5 core benchmarks at new defaults to check quality regressions on long-gen tasks. I'll take (2).
drew: Also consider enabling prefetched KV eviction heuristic (prefetch_kv_eviction=soft) for this model; it helps when many long sequences concurrently allocate.
anya: Filed PR: r/inference-config#412 — includes route default change, kv_trim flag, and microbatch recommendation. Link: https://git.redwood/r/412
ml-oncall: I'll monitor incidents channel and set alert on OOM rate >0.5% for this route for 24h post-rollout.
anya: TL;DR: mitigation works, perf impact acceptable. Next: run longer 24h canary with production traffic and full eval sweep. Will post follow-ups. :raised_hands:
